messages.subject: Re: NA/NaN argument error
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Thank you for this very interested topic about issues encountered when running Maaslin on R.

I am writing because I am encountering the same kind of issues when working at a Phylum level.

Error in if (0 < (resp <- attr(attr(frame, "terms"), "response"))) { :
  argument is of length zero

In addition: Warning messages:
1: In which(is.na <http://is.na>(as.numeric(lItemElement))) : NAs introduced by coercion
2: In which(is.na <http://is.na>(as.numeric(lItemElement))) : NAs introduced by coercion

In addition, when working on the Species level, I am encountering this other issue:

Error in if (0 < (resp <- attr(attr(frame, "terms"), "response"))) { :
  argument is of length zero
In addition: There were 23 warnings (use warnings() to see them)
> warnings()
Messages d'avis :

1: In which(is.na <http://is.na>(as.numeric(lItemElement))) : NAs introduced by coercion
2: In which(is.na <http://is.na>(as.numeric(lItemElement))) : NAs introduced by coercion

3: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
4: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
5: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
6: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
7: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
8: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
9: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
10: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
11: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
12: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
13: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
14: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
15: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
16: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
17: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
18: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
19: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
20: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
21: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
22: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced
23: In sqrt(s) : NaNs produced

I have checked and rechecked my PCL and config files (attached for both Species and Phylum levels), but I cannot seem to figure out where the error does come from.

I would be very grateful for any kind of help!

On Wednesday, February 14, 2018 at 7:14:34 PM UTC+1, Himel Mallick wrote:

> Hi Wenjie,
>
> The config file should be .config file rather a .txt file. You need to specify the random effects in the R code itself (e.g. strRandomCovariates = 'id' in your version of the code). The only change I made in the PCL file is optional. You can avoid it but for debugging purposes, I wanted to test the code with a well-known naming convention.

messages.subject_clean: Using Maaslin on R: how to install Maaslin?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Valentin,

Did you make sure the downloaded file (I recommend the latest version 0.0.5, available from https://bitbucket.org/biobakery/maaslin/) is located in your working directory? If not, can you confirm and try again?

Many thanks,
Himel

messages.subject: Re: NA/NaN argument error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Valentin,

Related to the issue above, did you try the latest version of MaAsLin (i.e. 0.0.5)? If not, could you follow the instructions in https://bitbucket.org/biobakery/maaslin/ to install the latest version of MaAsLin and try again? Please note that you need to install the following R packages before installing MaAsLin: fagricolae, gam (version 1.14), gamlss, gbm, glmnet, inlinedocs, logging, MASS, nlme (version 3.1-127), optparse, outliers, penalized, pscl, robustbase. Please let me know if you still have issues after installing the latest version.

Many thanks,
Himel

messages.subject: Run Maaslin for specific taxonomic levels
messages.subject_clean: Run Maaslin for specific taxonomic levels
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Is there an option that allow me to run Maaslin for some specific taxonomic level? For example, I want to find association at the genus level using the output of Metaphlan2. Do I need to filter my metaphlan file by myself removing all lines in unwanted taxonomic levels, or there is way doing that using Maaslin?

I really appreciate all your help.

Best,
Francislon Silva
Ph.D. Student in Bioinformatics
Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais - Brasil

messages.subject: Re: Run Maaslin for specific taxonomic levels
messages.subject_clean: Run Maaslin for specific taxonomic levels
messages.body_plain:
Hi Francislon,

Currently, MaAsLin does not have this option, but you can check out the R package microbiomics <https://github.com/tvatanen/microbiomics/>, which has a function for reading specific taxonomic level from your Metaphlan2 table, that can be used in conjunction with MaAsLin in R. Hope that helps.

Many thanks,
Himel

Dear Himel and Maaslin community,

I have an additional question regarding the forcing of predictors in Maaslin.

In the Maaslin help documentation on R, it is stated that:
strForcedPredictors : Metadata features that will be forced into the model seperated by commas. These features must be listed in the read.config file. Example '-F Metadata2,Metadata6,Metadata10'.

With the PCL file attached and knowing that I want to force AGE, SEX, BV0, and Tob into my model, I have tried to modify my CONFIG file to make it look like this:

Matrix: Metadata
Read_PCL_Rows: -Tob

Matrix: Abundance
Read_PCL_Rows: Bacteroidetes-

-F AGE,SEX,BV0,Tob

And my R-code to look like that:

Maaslin('CoarsePhylum.pcl','maaslin_output',strInputConfig='CoarsePhylum_maaslin.read.config', dSignificanceLevel=0.10, strForcedPredictors=AGE,SEX,BVO,Tob)

But I get an error message saying that my AGE object is not found...

My take on that would be that either my R code or my CONFIG file (or both...) have one or multiple errors... Could you please enlighten me as per the correct syntax to force predictors?
I would be very grateful!

Thanks a lot for your help and support!

Valentin

messages.body_plain:
Hi Valentin,

Since you are calling the function within R, you need to specify the forced predictors using standard vector notation in R. For your specific example, this will translate to strForcedPredictors=c(‘AGE’, ‘SEX’, ‘BVO’, ‘Tob’) in your MaAsLin function. The comma-separated values will be required when you will call MaAsLin from the command line. Hope this helps.

Many thanks,
Himel
